segments.title: Chương 49: 0049 【Đẩy mạnh Trần Quý Lương】
segments.content:
Magic City.

Ai Shen Garden.

This is the location of the Shanghai Writers' Association.

The editorial departments of several magazines, such as Harvest, Sprout, and Shanghai Literature, are all located here.

On the second floor of the Sprout magazine office, contest submissions were piled up like mountains.

They had long since run out of room inside, even filling the balcony outside.

There were only a little over sixty thousand contestants this year, but the number of manuscripts reached over 400,000, which meant an average of seven submissions per person.

Chen Guiliang only submitted four, which was already very conservative.

With over 400,000 preliminary submissions, judging had become a physical chore, so naturally, they couldn't trouble the famous authors with it.

Step one: rough screening.

This was carried out by regular editors, who would select about ten thousand submissions of a certain standard.

Step two: detailed review.

This was carried out by the editor-in-chief, deputy editor-in-chief, and senior editors, as well as second-rate writers and literary critics residing in Magic City. From those ten thousand submissions, 200 contestants would be selected to enter the semi-finals.

Famous authors of Yu Hua and Su Tong's caliber would not participate in the judging at this stage; they would only appear during the semi-finals.

In this world, whenever the word "profit" is involved, someone is bound to come and cut the cake.

The New Concept Composition Contest was no exception.

For example, certain well-known high schools, especially those local to Magic City, could recommend students for the competition.

Of course, they still had to go through the motions.

The usual procedure was like this: a master-level Chinese teacher would help their student "polish" their work, then recommend it in the school's name. A high-quality preliminary essay was thus produced, guaranteed to pass the rough screening and with a very high chance of entering the semi-finals.

Once in the semi-finals, an honorable mention was the minimum, and with luck, one could win second or third prize.

Although it couldn't earn extra points on the college entrance exam, nor could it guarantee admission to a prestigious university, having an award on one's resume could be leveraged for other things.

So, of those 200 semi-finalist spots, who knew how many were recommended candidates from famous high schools.

At this moment, the preliminary judging had already concluded.

Those eliminated manuscripts were tied into bundles of one hundred, with a sticker indicating "Group X, 100 manuscripts," and thrown in stacks on the editorial department's balcony.

They certainly couldn't be sold as scrap paper right away; it would take at least half a year to process them.

Zhao Yan and Hu Weishi were repeatedly reading the accepted essays.

First, they needed to select twenty or thirty outstanding pieces to be included in next year's "Selected Works from the New Concept Contest Winners." Second, they needed to pick a few promising candidates to be listed as key targets for Sprout's promotion and cultivation.

"This Li Haiyang's essay is quite good. The writing is very sophisticated," Zhao Yan said.

Zhao Yan was the editor-in-chief's own son, a senior editor and reporter at Sprout, and a future famous suspense novelist. Currently, he often hung out on Longkong, and through Longkong, he had published a web novel.

He could be considered an ancient web novel guru.

Hu Weishi said, "I called Li Haiyang yesterday. He said he's brainstorming a full-length novel. He's already finished the beginning, called something like 'The Zha Biliang Assault Incident.' But he's a busy high school senior and plans to continue writing after the college entrance exam."

Zhao Yan read a few dozen more essays and sighed, "Although the number of submissions has skyrocketed this year, the quality is in continuous decline. Most of the articles are cookie-cutter, with no appeal whatsoever."

Hu Weishi commented, "They're too utilitarian, all just New Concept's version of the eight-legged essay. It's already violated the original intention of our contest."

The main principle of the New Concept Composition Contest was to be "new," yet the submissions received in recent years were incredibly "old-fashioned."

Boiling it down, there were mainly two writing styles.

One was to imitate Han Han, feigning maturity, which was really just showing off one's reading and being a smart aleck. They'd quote obscure books or famous sayings, write some childish text pretending to be profound, and offer so-called scathing satire on social issues.

The other was to imitate Guo Xiaosi and play up the melancholy, forcing sorrow for the sake of a new verse.

The number of submissions that could break free from these two styles was few and far between, and those that were also well-written were even rarer.

When the editors were judging, faced with hundreds of thousands of manuscripts, it was no different from panning for gold in a pile of shit!

Whenever they came across a piece with a bit of originality, they had to read it over and over again to cleanse their eyes. As for the trashy manuscripts, it was over in a few seconds. An extra glance would make their hearts ache with exhaustion.

"Take a look at Chen Guiliang's manuscripts," Hu Weishi tossed over a stack of papers. "Four articles. One in four-six parallelism, one sci-fi short story, one piece of rural prose, and one reading notes essay. All of them passed the rough screening, which is very impressive."

Zhao Yan laughed, "People still write in parallelism these days?"

"I even suspect he might have had someone ghostwrite it, or maybe he just copied it from somewhere," Hu Weishi said, adding, "He's an alumnus of Guo Xiaosi's high school."

Hearing that he was an alumnus of Guo Xiaosi, Zhao Yan couldn't help but frown.

Chen Guiliang's four articles were held together by the review team with a paperclip.

When Zhao Yan read the piece, "A Proclamation Denouncing America's Invasion of Iraq," he immediately chuckled, "It really doesn't sound like a high school student's writing. A Chinese teacher must have polished it. These Chinese teachers, they're just banking on their students winning awards to make a name for themselves."

The full-score college entrance exam essay from two years ago, "The Death of Red Hare," was also written in classical Chinese, and its author was even admitted to Nanjing Normal University by special exception.

But that was just classical vernacular.

This piece by Chen Guiliang, however, was in four-six parallelism!

Of course, it was hard to judge the level of difficulty.

After all, "The Death of Red Hare" was written during the college entrance exam, where time was extremely limited, and most people wouldn't have the guts.

Below Chen Guiliang's article, there was also Hu Weishi's comment: "It is quite rare for a high school student to have such a command of classical Chinese. 'One hundred thousand souls become new ghosts, a thousand years of civilization fall into the nine abysses'—this line captures the cruelty of war and highlights the anti-war core of this essay."

After finishing the first piece, Zhao Yan read the second, and his eyes lit up, "It's actually cyberpunk!"

Hu Weishi asked, "Isn't it sci-fi? What's cyberpunk?"

Zhao Yan said, "Cyberpunk is a genre of science fiction. The Matrix is cyberpunk."

"Is this kind of memory deletion, customization, replacement, and sale common in cyberpunk novels?" Hu Weishi asked.

Zhao Yan shook his head, "I don't think it's very common. A pity it's just a short story. It would be great if it could be expanded into a full-length novel."

He then wrote down his comment: "The imagination is strange and fantastic, and reading it is bone-chilling. Although it is a five-thousand-word short story, it outlines a vivid and deformed future world."

Then he looked at the remaining two pieces, and both had comments.

In the past two or three years, fewer and fewer articles had been deemed worthy of a comment.

Even among the articles compiled into the "Selected Works from the New Concept Contest Winners," more than a third did not receive any comments from the judges.

Because the quality was just so-so, and writing a comment felt like a waste of ink.

"Knock, knock, knock."

An editor knocked on the open door of the room, "Editor Hu, the editor-in-chief would like to see you."

"Coming."

Holding a few manuscripts, Hu Weishi walked straight towards the editor-in-chief's office.

"Knock, knock, knock!"

"Come in."

Inside the editor-in-chief's office sat two people.

One was Sprout's editor-in-chief, Zhao Changtian.

The other was the general secretary of the New Concept Contest, Li Qigang.

Hu Weishi waved away the smoke in the air, walked in, and joked, "Are you two praying to the gods? How many cigarettes have you smoked?"

"No more smoking, out of respect for our female comrade." Zhao Changtian stood up to open the window wider.

Hu Weishi asked, "What difficulty have you run into?"

Li Qigang, with a grim expression, said, "The major universities are further lowering their cooperation standards. There are only two left that are still willing to grant admission without an exam, and they are both arts colleges. Next year, the exam-free admission will be completely canceled!"

"Is it that serious?" Hu Weishi was taken aback.

Editor-in-Chief Zhao Changtian nodded, "Independent admissions are being further regulated, and all universities must implement the policy. This year's competition has already started, so it's inconvenient for those universities to go back on their word at the last minute, and they understand our difficulties. So, the schools will still send people over, but it'll just be for show."

"What's the attitude of Tsinghua and Peking University?" Li Qigang asked.

Zhao Changtian said, "They might lower the admission score by 10 to 30 points. They still need to discuss exactly how much. In fact, how many points they lower it by isn't the key. The key is whether they will give any spots. So what if they agree to lower it by 200 points? They can choose not to give a single spot, or they can add an interview stage to screen people out."

The actual situation was even more complicated.

For example, back in the day with Guo Xiaosi, Xiamen University had already agreed to admit him by special exception, as long as he passed the Tier 1 cutoff score. Guo Xiaosi exceeded the Tier 1 cutoff by a full 54 points, but because his composition score was only 30, Xiamen University went back on its word and didn't admit him.

These were all just excuses. The truth was very simple: the university changed its mind at the last minute due to public opinion and policy influence.

Hu Weishi asked again, "What about the other key universities?"

Zhao Changtian said, "Some require passing the key university cutoff line, some just need to pass the undergraduate line, and for others, it's about exceeding the key university line by a certain number of points. The New Concept Composition Contest is finished next year. Without the gimmick of guaranteed admission to prestigious universities, there will be fewer and fewer contestants, and the media won't pay it much attention."

This situation arose because the public controversy was too great, and the competition itself was becoming increasingly lackluster.

Moreover, the state was further regulating the college entrance exam, guaranteed admissions, and independent admissions.

The triggering event was the leak of this year's college entrance exam math paper, which ushered in a series of reforms for college entrance exams and admissions.

Because of the college entrance exam reforms and the strict investigation of various chaotic phenomena, a whole lot of dirty laundry would be aired next summer.

For example, a teacher from a certain school proactively contacted a candidate, saying that as long as their college entrance exam score wasn't too far off, they could be admitted by paying ten thousand yuan for each point they were short.

And for another example, a top art academy was proven to have engaged in favoritism and fraud during its art exams, and they did it so blatantly they didn't even bother to hide it.

There was also a university that was even featured on "Focus Report," for forcing a candidate to pay 100,000 yuan for admission. The final investigation revealed that a total of 7 national defense students had been extorted for a total of 550,000 yuan by teachers at that school.

The above were just a few examples, and they involved prestigious universities!

The major universities lowering their cooperation standards and giving up on guaranteed admission for New Concept Contest winners were purely collateral damage from the college entrance exam reforms.

Li Qigang sighed, "We must think of something."

"Regulating admissions is the general trend. We can't try to stop an avalanche," Zhao Changtian said.

Li Qigang thought for a moment, "Then let's organize our own event and get the media to hype it up."

Zhao Changtian asked, "What are you thinking?"

Li Qigang explained, "Let's invite back all the past first-prize winners, especially celebrities like Han Han, Guo Xiaosi, and Zhang Yueran. Have them engage in a dialogue with famous authors like Yu Hua and Su Tong to discuss the development trends of contemporary Chinese literature."

"That could work," Zhao Changtian nodded.

Li Qigang added, "We can also select a few promising winners from this year's competition to attend."

"You want to create a new Han Han or Guo Xiaosi?" Zhao Changtian asked.

Li Qigang said, "Han Han has gone off to play with race cars, Guo Xiaosi is busy running his magazine, and Zhang Yueran can't generate enough buzz. Besides, Guo Xiaosi is mired in a plagiarism scandal. We must promote a new person to maintain the visibility of Sprout and New Concept."

Zhao Changtian said to Hu Weishi, "The task of scouting for good prospects will be up to you, Xiao Hu."

Hu Weishi took out Chen Guiliang's four articles, "As it happens, there's a good candidate. He's also an alumnus of Guo Xiaosi's high school."

Li Qigang praised, "That's a good gimmick. We can have them, as senior and junior schoolmates, have a chat in front of the media."

After Zhao Changtian finished reading the four articles, he said worriedly, "These articles were probably tutored by a teacher."

He stopped just short of saying they were ghostwritten.

Hu Weishi said, "So we'll have to see his performance in the finals."

Li Qigang said, "During the finals, we'll pay close attention to this... what's his name?"

"Chen Guiliang," Hu Weishi said.

Li Qigang said, "Right, we'll focus on Chen Guiliang. As long as he has real talent and writes a good essay in the finals, we can promote him heavily."
